title: Bounded-size generators for acyclic complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For an object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ its *size* $|M|$ is the cardinality of the set of subobjects of $M$ [lem-pur-kinjective-set-iso-classes-bounded-size]. There exists a cardinal $\kappa$ such that for every acyclic (as in [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$) cochain complex $M^\bullet$ in $\mathcal A$ (cochain complexes defined as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$): (1) if $M^\bullet\neq0$, there is a nonzero subcomplex $N^\bullet\subset M^\bullet$ which is bounded above, acyclic, and has $|N^n|\le\kappa$ for all $n$; (2) there is a surjection of complexes $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ with each $M_i^\bullet$ bounded above, acyclic, and $|M_i^n|\le\kappa$ for all $n$.

proof.text: Choose a generator $U$ and let $c(\lambda)=|\bigoplus_{\lambda}U|$. Set $\kappa=\sup_{n\ge1}c^n(|U|)$. For a morphism $\psi:U\to M^n$ it is enough to construct a bounded-above acyclic subcomplex through which $\psi$ factors, with the stated termwise bounds.

Start with $N^n=\operatorname{Im}(\psi)$, $N^{n+1}=\operatorname{Im}(U\xrightarrow{\psi}M^n\to M^{n+1})$, and $N^m=0$ for $m\ge n+2$; images of $U$ have size at most $|U|$. Inductively, for some $k\le n$ suppose subobjects $N^m\subset M^m$ for $m\ge k$ have been constructed with (i) $d(N^m)\subset N^{m+1}$ for $m\ge k$, (ii) $\operatorname{Im}(N^{m-1}\to N^m)=\Ker(N^m\to N^{m+1})$ for $m\ge k+1$ (exactness of $N^\bullet$, not of $M^\bullet$), and (iii) $|N^m|\le c^{\max\{n-m,0\}}(|U|)$ for $m\ge k$. Because $M^\bullet$ is acyclic, $d\circ d=0$ and $\Ker(N^k\to N^{k+1})\subset\Ker(d^k_M)=\operatorname{Im}(d^{k-1}_M)$, the subobject $d^{-1}(\Ker(N^k\to N^{k+1}))\subset M^{k-1}$ surjects onto that kernel. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-surjection-bounded-size] to this surjection to choose $N^{k-1}\subset d^{-1}(\Ker(N^k\to N^{k+1}))$ surjecting onto $\Ker(N^k\to N^{k+1})$; since $|\Ker(N^k\to N^{k+1})|\le|N^k|$ and $c$ is monotone, $|N^{k-1}|\le c^{n-k+1}(|U|)$. Then (i), (ii), (iii) hold with $k-1$ in place of $k$ (exactness at $n+1$ and $n$ holds by construction of $N^{n+1}$ and at $k$ by the choice of $N^{k-1}$). Descending induction over all $k\le n$ produces a subcomplex $N^\bullet$, bounded above, exact in every degree (hence acyclic), with all terms of size at most $\kappa$, through which $\psi$ factors.

If $M^\bullet\ne0$, choose a degree and a morphism from the generator whose image is nonzero. The construction in the preceding step then gives a nonzero bounded-above acyclic subcomplex with $|N^m|\le\kappa$, proving clause (1).

Apply the construction to every morphism $U\to M^n$ in every degree. Since $U$ is a generator, these images jointly generate each term, and the resulting bounded-above acyclic subcomplexes map to $M^\bullet$. Taking their coproduct gives an epimorphism $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i^\bullet\twoheadrightarrow M^\bullet$; each $M_i^\bullet$ is bounded above, acyclic, and has all terms of size at most $\kappa$. This proves clause (2).
